c_macaquet.text: It looks at your bag, then at you, then at your bag. You hold on to it a little tighter.

gib_keeper_chat.text: They're not tame, they're not pets and they do not want your biscuits. Feeding them is illegal and a fine of up to £4,000 is possible.
They'll still try. A big male once took a lady's handbag, undid the zip and ate her lipstick. She wasn't the only one.

gib_tunnel_guide.text: Sergeant-Major Henry Ince is credited with the first tunnel. He got the idea from a crowded gun position that wasn't wide enough for the guns, and decided to open up the rock.
Right up here is the Notch, and St George's Hall, a gun gallery as big as a cathedral. In all there are more tunnels in the Rock than there are public roads.

gib_cave_guide.text: St Michael's Cave has a concert hall in it. Sometimes people play the cave's own stalactites with a mallet.
In the old days they said it was bottomless and went all the way down under the Strait. Nobody has found the bottom, and nobody who goes looking is back for tea.

gib_birder.text: In autumn, when the wind's right, the sky above Europa Point is full of kites and honey buzzards. They hang there for hours, just waiting for the right thermal.
If the weather's wrong, they gather and wait. You'll see ten thousand birds on a good day, and one very tired birdwatcher.

gib_priest_europa.text: The Shrine of Our Lady of Europe is a chapel at the southern tip. Sailors prayed there, and still do, for a safe passage through the Strait.
The chapel was once a mosque and then a church, and it's now a peaceful place of both. The light through the window is lovely at dusk.
